items.title: John Levy interviewed by Monk Rowe, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: I got a call to come down to Birdland to work, finish out a week with Buddy Rich. Buddy Rich had a big band.

ctx.x: Oh, yeah, and that really ticked me off because everything was backwards, you know. We didn’t get paid on time, and when you had to travel no arrangements were being made for it, and nothing. Everybody was on their own, you know, and I didn’t like it. So

when they left to go to California, I decided I was going to quit. So I left that group and this was about the time that I was just sort of like floating around. I got a call to come down to Birdland to work, finish out a week with Buddy Rich. Buddy Rich had a big band. So I went down to Birdland and worked the week with Buddy Rich and George Shearing was playing opposite Buddy Rich. In other words, in those days, in Birdland, there might be three or four different acts. And in this case I think it was George…

I would think that, you know, for managing musicians, you had a really valuable experience doing everything that they do, you know, because now you know what kind of travel they need to have, what kind of arrangements need to be made.

items.title: John Levy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I finished out the week with Buddy Rich.

ctx.x: That was in – that was at Birdland – no, at the – they called it the Clique. That was the Clique, before the name changed to Birdland. It was the Clique. Jimmy was working there with Sarah. Naturally, when something came up where a bass player was needed, he called me. I was at home doing nothing. [He said], “Can you come down and play with Buddy Rich? This bass player had to leave.” Fine. Picked up a bass, went down, start playing with Buddy Rich. I finished the week up. Buddy was on the last week of the…
